source: IRS Revenue Procedure 2024-40 (published Oct 22, 2024), with standard deductions as raised by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21, signed July 4, 2025). Social Security wage base per SSA's Oct 2024 announcement.
notes: All bracket thresholds are TAXABLE income (after standard/itemized deductions), not gross income. Rates apply to income earned Jan 1 - Dec 31, 2025, reported on returns filed in early 2026. Bracket `min` values follow the IRS table convention (one dollar above the previous `max`); the loader in lib/taxData.ts snaps them down to the previous `max` so no dollar falls through a boundary. A past year's figures are final: scripts/update-tax-data.mjs only ever writes the newest year.

long_term_capital_gains_and_qualified_di.notes: Applies to assets held more than 1 year and to qualified dividends. Thresholds are taxable income (ordinary income + gains, after deductions), stacked on top of ordinary income. Short-term gains are taxed at ordinary income rates above, not these rates. Collectibles (28%) and unrecaptured Sec. 1250 real estate depreciation recapture (25%) are separate rates not covered here.

net_investment_income_tax.name: Net Investment Income Tax (NIIT)
net_investment_income_tax.notes: Under IRC section 1411. Applies to the lesser of net investment income or the excess of MAGI over the threshold. On top of, not instead of, ordinary/capital gains rates. Thresholds are fixed by statute since 2013 and are NOT inflation-adjusted.

additional_medicare_tax.name: Additional Medicare Tax
additional_medicare_tax.notes: Under IRC section 3101(b)(2). Applies to wages/self-employment income above the threshold, on top of the standard 1.45% Medicare tax. Thresholds are fixed by statute since 2013 and are NOT inflation-adjusted. Based on wages, not filing-status-adjusted taxable income.

personal_exemption.notes: Eliminated by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (2017) and made permanent at $0 by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA).

self_employment_tax.name: Self-Employment Tax (SECA)
self_employment_tax.notes: IRC 1401/1402. Charged on `net_earnings_factor` of net self-employment profit. The Social Security portion is capped at `social_security_wage_base`, and W-2 wages consume that cap first; the Medicare portion is uncapped. Half the resulting tax is deductible above the line under IRC 164(f). No tax is due if net earnings fall below `minimum_net_earnings`.

fica_employee.name: FICA (employee share)
fica_employee.notes: Withheld from W-2 wages under IRC 3101. The employer pays a matching share, which is not the employee's cost and is not counted here. Social Security stops at the same wage base as SECA.

social_security_benefits.name: Taxability of Social Security benefits
social_security_benefits.notes: IRC 86. Provisional income = AGI excluding benefits + tax-exempt interest + half the benefits. Below `base_amounts`, nothing is taxable. Between the two thresholds, the taxable share tops out at 50%. Above `adjusted_base_amounts` it tops out at 85%, computed as 85% of the overage plus the lesser of `adjustment_amounts` or half the benefits. None of these figures has ever been indexed — they are fixed at their 1983/1993 values. `married_separate` carries $0 because IRC 86(c)(1)(C) zeroes the base for a spouse who lived with their partner at any point in the year; a separated filer living apart all year gets the single amounts instead, which this calculator does not model.

child_tax_credit.name: Child Tax Credit
child_tax_credit.notes: IRC 24 as amended by OBBBA, which raised the credit to $2,200 for tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2024. Non-refundable against income tax; up to `refundable_limit` per child (per Rev. Proc. 2024-40) can be refundable as the Additional Child Tax Credit, which this calculator does NOT pay out — it only reduces tax to zero. Reduced by `phaseout_per` for each `phaseout_step` of MAGI (or fraction of one) above the threshold. `other_dependent_credit` covers dependents who are not qualifying children and is never refundable.

charitable_deduction_limits.notes: IRC 170(b)(1)(A) — cash gifts to 501(c)(3) public charities are deductible up to this share of AGI. Excess carries forward up to five years. `agi_floor` is 0: OBBBA's 0.5%-of-AGI floor on itemized charitable deductions starts with tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2025, so a 2025 gift is deductible from the first dollar.

itemized_deduction_limit.name: Limitation on itemized deductions
itemized_deduction_limit.notes: `benefit_rate_cap` is null: OBBBA's IRC 68 cap, which holds the value of an itemized deduction to 35% for top-bracket filers, starts with tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2025. A 2025 itemized deduction is worth the full marginal rate.
